subject: PayGrid model-fit eval: parity thresholds & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Nguyen <olivia@paygrid.com>, Rajesh Patel <rajesh@paygrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: PayGrid discovery recap + proposed evaluation plan

Hi Olivia / Rajesh,

Thanks again for the call today  great context on the transaction-matching flow and the latency constraints for real-time reconciliation (p95 < 150ms on reads, async batch ok for overnight jobs). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Scope: model fit for: 1) customer-facing reconciliation assistant (short text explanation & suggested match), 2) nightly batch reranking for unmatched transactions.
- Success criteria (initial): precision@1 >= 85% for the assistant; rerank NDCG@10 improvement > 20% vs your current baseline.
- Data: sample dataset of ~50k historical matches (anonymized) would be ideal for our first parity eval.
- Security: SOC2 in place; we can run the eval in our private tenant or on your VPC-connected environment depending on preference.

Next steps I propose: 
1) We share the prompt set and a short benchmark harness (attached) + recommended open models to evaluate.
2) You share a 5k-10k anonymized sample (or we can point to a secure S3 link).
3) We run a 2-week model-fit eval and share parity results and regression analysis.

I've attached the prompt set we discussed and a short outline of recommended models. Aditya and Ben are cc'ed to help with technical setup and timing.

If that sounds good, can you confirm the sample cadence (daily vs weekly) and who on your side will share the data link?

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai

Attachment: paygrid-eval-prompt-set.csv

From: Olivia Nguyen <olivia@paygrid.com>

Cc: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@paygrid.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PayGrid discovery recap + proposed evaluation plan

Marissa  thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers: 

- We can provide a 10k anonymized sample (S3 link) by EOD Thursday.
- Preference is to run the first eval in your private tenant if possible; our security team prefers not to provision new VPC connections for a short pilot.
- On the success criteria: the team is particularly sensitive to precision on high-value transactions (>$1k). If you can include a stratified metric for that slice, that would be helpful.

One question: what open models do you recommend starting with for parity checks vs our current proprietary baseline? Interested in both cost and latency tradeoffs.

Olivia
Head of Product, PayGrid

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Nguyen <olivia@paygrid.com>, Rajesh Patel <rajesh@paygrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PayGrid discovery recap + proposed evaluation plan

Hi Olivia  great, thanks. Quick answers inline and attached a concise recommendation doc.

Q: which open models to start with?
A: For parity vs a proprietary transaction-matching baseline we typically run a three-tiered sweep: 
  - 1) LLM family A (efficient 7B quantized)  cost-friendly, low-latency; good for first pass and prompt-heavy heuristics.
  - 2) LLM family B (13B mixed precision)  better single-turn reasoning; expect noticeable quality uplift on ambiguous matches.
  - 3) LLM family C (70B/finetuned variant)  parity candidate for higher-end proprietary baselines; higher cost and latency but often required to hit strict acceptance thresholds.

We attach "redwood-recommended-models.md" with concrete model names (open checkpoints), expected token latency on our Dedicated configs, and rough cost-per-1000-token estimates. We've also included the prompt set CSV and a sample benchmark harness link.

On stratified metrics: absolutely  we'll compute precision@1 segmented by transaction amount buckets (0-100, 100-1k, >1k). We'll also run a calibration check for high-value transactions to minimize false positives.

Regarding environment: running the eval in our private tenant is fine; we'll spin up an isolated job and provide access logs for your security team. Please send the S3 link and a short ACL list for access.

Proposed timeline: 48-72h to stand up the eval once we have data + 7-10 days to run the sweep and gather parity/regression metrics. Deliverables: parity report (PDF), per-prompt failure cases, recommended model/profile for production, and an action plan for a staged rollout (canary + fallback).

Next call? I suggest a 30-min sync next Wed to review initial parity results  propose Wed 11 Mar 2026 10:00am PT. If that works, Ben / Aditya / Laura will join for technical Q&A.

Thanks  attaching results template and the parity benchmark PDF stub.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-recommended-models.md; parity-benchmark-results.pdf; paygrid-eval-prompt-set.csv

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: parity thresholds & regen concerns for PayGrid eval

Team  quick internal note before the eval kicks off. Key technical points to watch: 

- Regression detection: we should baseline on both precision@1 and a per-prompt quality delta. For transactions labeled borderline by PayGrid, include a manual review sample to estimate false positive rates.
- Parity threshold proposal: for us to recommend an open-model as a production replacement, require: precision@1 >= 0.85 AND delta_vs_baseline <= 5% on recall across high-value bucket. If not met, recommend hybrid approach (open model for assist + rerank with your current baseline).
- Infrastructure: run the 7B/13B/70B sweep in parallel on Dedicated to keep latency profiles consistent. Log per-token latencies and tail percentiles.
- Prompt stability: include prompt perturbation tests (paraphrases, truncated context)  sometimes small prompt shifts surface brittle failure modes.

I'm attaching a short checklist and the parity result template (stub). Laura, can you validate the Dedicated config we plan to use and confirm expected p95 token latencies? Ben  can you coordinate the onboarding access to their S3 bucket?

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: parity-benchmark-results.pdf

Thanks again  excited to run the sweep.

Marissa
